page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9B45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 30.0 GB of system memory, which allocates 1.88 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The platform incorporates AVX-512 vector support including VNNI and BF16 instructions, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional single-threaded capabilities. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core processing, Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and text processing. Light language model inference also shows strong throughput on small models, delivering 424.39 tokens per second on 135M parameter text generation. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation via Clang, register in the middle fifty percent of cloud servers. Memory throughput for uncached large blocks registers at 53.46 GB/sec for reads and 34.08 GB/sec for writes.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on memory density and storage. With approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance is constrained for large in-memory databases or sprawling multi-gigabyte datasets. Furthermore, no local NVMe storage is bundled, requiring reliance on remote persistent disks for disk I/O operations. Without discrete GPU accelerators, hardware acceleration is limited to CPU-native instruction sets.

This hardware balance positions the c4d-highcpu-16 effectively for CPU-bound tasks that prioritize high per-core execution speeds over memory scale. Primary workload fits include batch processing, compression pipelines, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight inferencing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-16 provides 16 dedicated vCPUs and 30.0 GB of system memory powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor across 8 physical cores. Designed with a compute-heavy profile of 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, it features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 instruction set extensions. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU throughput, leading performance in single-threaded data compression, and strong handling of small-model text inference. Multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth align within average cloud server tiers. The server includes no bundled local storage and lacks GPU accelerators, making it reliant on external storage solutions. This hardware allocation serves compute-intensive workloads that benefit from rapid per-thread performance, including build compilation, data transformation, batch compute jobs, and lightweight web serving.
